title: E1 Ask quality harness -- pre-registered protocol

supersedes.receiptsProducedUnderV1: none (fixture runs only; no live receipt exists)
why: M1: v1 numeric extraction read the day of a date and form names as numbers ('June 30, 2025' -> 30, '10-K' -> 10), so a correct answer restating its question scored NOT_A_SINGLE_VALUE. v2 strips dates, filing-form names and Item/Note/Part/Schedule/Exhibit references before extraction.

M2: v1 had no metric for abstention on answerable questions or gold-span recall, so an answerer abstaining on everything lost nothing on any registered row and E2's 'no loss of correct answers' gate could pass vacuously. v2 adds abstained_over_answerable.<set> and gold_span_recall.<set>.
m3: v1 OTHER_YEAR shifted dates by whole years, producing a non-existent J&J fiscal-year end (2013-12-28). v2 uses the filer's real fiscal-year period from companyfacts.
m4: v2 adds citation_precision_4plus_digit_spans.<set> because 3-digit gold spans collide by accident.

m5/m8: question files now record companyfacts/submissions payload sha256s and name the span index htmlCharOffset (UTF-16 code units). These change the question-set bytes, hence the new sha256s below; the 400 numeric questions themselves (ids, text, gold) are unchanged.
Revised before any live receipt, after independent review REVIEW-E1-R1, so no result informed the change.

lane: Market-No.1 program W1-L4, workstream E, item E1 (PROGRAM-2026-11-04.md §4.E)
claim: None. This protocol makes no quality claim. A number exists only as a receipt produced by run_eval.mjs against the question sets pinned below, and is read with its denominator.

baseline.note: Both paths answer with answerMode evidence_excerpts: the answer is the concatenated text of the cited evidence and no model generates anything. Every per-question row records which retrievalPath answered. The adapter refuses any other answerMode and refuses production hosts.
baseline.corpus: Each corpusRef sec-10k:<CIK> is the two pinned 10-K primary documents of that filer (questions/xbrl-numeric.json#filers, url + sha256), uploaded as one collection; the operator supplies the corpusRef -> collectionId map at run time.

questionSets.source: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts + the filings' inline XBRL; filers Coca-Cola (0000021344), Johnson & Johnson (0000200406), Microsoft (0000789019), Procter & Gamble (0000080424); two 10-Ks each, 50 questions per filing
OTHER_COMPANY 120 (4 corpora x 3 other filers x 10) + OTHER_YEAR 40 (4 corpora x 10, each asked of a real reported fiscal-year period from companyfacts); rules in the file's unanswerableRules

Human-written questions on the A4 proof-run documents, target n >= 30. Today the file is a template with 5 agent-written worked examples (humanVerified=false). It is frozen by replacing this entry's sha256 and n in a new PREREG revision before any run that reports it.

xbrlMatchingRule.reference: masterplan v4 §16.4 (the program text cites it as 'v4 §17.x'; the SEC corpus rule lives in §16.4): XBRL is a ground-truth candidate only after the filing's context, unit and period are matched exactly
xbrlMatchingRule.rule: A companyfacts fact (us-gaap concept, unit in USD | USD/shares | shares, accn = the pinned filing, form 10-K, end = the filing's reportDate, duration 350-380 days or instant) becomes a question only when the filing's inline XBRL carries a VISIBLE ix:nonFraction (outside ix:header) with the same concept, a non-dimensional context with the same start/end or instant, a unit whose measures map to the same unit string, and displayed digits x 10^scale x sign equal to the companyfacts value.
xbrlMatchingRule.drops: val = 0; no visible matching span; every matching span has fewer than 3 digits; two facts that render the same question text with different values. Counts per filing are in questions/xbrl-numeric.json#filers[].filings[].stats.
xbrlMatchingRule.sample: per filing, order the surviving facts by sha256(accession|concept|unit|start|end) and keep the first 50

split: Every question carries split = calibration | holdout, from the parity of sha256(id)'s first 32 bits. E2 sets its coverage threshold on calibration and is judged on holdout (PROGRAM §4.E E2).

scoring.abstention: abstained = the answerer reported abstained, or it returned an empty answer and zero citations. evidence_excerpts: abstained = status != grounded (EVIDENCE_EXCEEDS_ANSWER_LIMIT abstains with citations kept; it is an abstention).
scoring.correctAnswerable: numeric question: correct = not abstained AND numeric exact match. text question: correct = not abstained AND the normalized answer contains one of gold.acceptableAnswers (containment over-credits long answers; the human adjudication column is authoritative where it exists).
scoring.numericExactMatch: Before extraction, text that names something rather than states an amount is removed: month-name dates with a day ('June 30, 2025', 'Dec. 28'), ISO and slash dates, filing-form names (10-K, 10-KT, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F, 6-K, S-1, optionally /A) and Item/Note/Part/Schedule/Exhibit references (score.ts NON_AMOUNT_PATTERNS). The answer's value is its structured numeric when present, otherwise the single distinct number its text states (scale words thousand/million/billion/trillion applied; parentheses or a leading minus negate; a bare 1900-2100 integer is a year and ignored). Several distinct numbers = NOT_A_SINGLE_VALUE = no match. A unit the answer states must equal the gold unit. Value matches when |answer - gold| < 0.5 x 10^-decimals (XBRL decimals); decimals INF/null requires equality. Consequence stated in advance: evidence_excerpts returns passages, not a value, so its numeric exact match is expected to be near 0 by construction; that is the baseline being measured, not a defect of the scorer.
scoring.citationContainsGold: A citation contains the gold span when its text contains one of gold.spans: a numeric span (digits, commas, dots) must appear as a whole number (1,394,328 does not contain 394,328); any other span is a normalized substring. For the evidence_excerpts adapter the citation text is the route's 420-character excerpt preview, so a gold span later in a long chunk is not seen. Matching is on the full display span as a whole number, never a sub-span. 3-digit spans recur by accident across a filing's tables (133 of the 400 v1 gold spans), so citation precision is also reported on the stratum of questions whose gold spans all have >= 4 digits.
scoring.latency: client-observed milliseconds per question for the live adapter (fetch start to response); simulated for the fixture

metrics.denominator: all citations returned for answerable xbrl-numeric questions
all citations returned for answerable xbrl-numeric questions whose gold spans are all non-numeric or >= 4 digits

metrics.numerator: answerable xbrl-numeric questions with at least one citation containing a gold span

metrics.denominator: all citations returned for answerable human questions
all citations returned for answerable human questions whose gold spans are all non-numeric or >= 4 digits

metrics.numerator: answerable human questions with at least one citation containing a gold span

statistics.interval: Wilson score interval, 95%, z = 1.959963984540054, on every rate
statistics.zeroDenominator: value null and interval null, never 0
statistics.clustering: Citation precision counts citations, which cluster within questions; the Wilson interval treats them as independent and understates the uncertainty. Stated, not corrected.
statistics.pooling: Answerable metrics are reported per question set. No pooled figure across sets is computed (PROGRAM §4.E risk: XBRL questions may skew easy).
statistics.e2Gate: Any gate judged on this harness (E2) reads correct_over_answerable, abstained_over_answerable and gold_span_recall together with wrong_answer_over_unanswerable; a lower wrong-answer rate bought by abstaining on answerable questions is visible in abstained_over_answerable and gold_span_recall.

openItems: human set: n >= 30 human-written, humanVerified questions on the A4 documents; then pin sha256 and n here in a new PREREG revision
unanswerable OTHER_YEAR: absence is established against tagged XBRL contexts only; a person spot-checks a sample against the filings before the set is cited
OTHER_YEAR periods come from companyfacts annual 10-K durations; a person confirms the 40 against the filers' own reported fiscal-year ends when spot-checking
baseline receipt: no live run has been made. It needs the eight pinned 10-Ks uploaded to a non-production workspace as four collections and a workspace token
a run against production is not authorised by this protocol
